articles.title: Zero Latency Study: Location-Based VR Is the Most Wanted Attraction in Entertainment Venues
articles.summary: A landmark consumer study of 2,386 participants across five countries found that VR ranked first at 93% among attractions guests most want, ahead of arcades, bowling, escape rooms, mini golf, and laser tag. Critically, VR is the only major attraction category to show rising consumer pull since 2023. For FEC operators, this presents a clear gap opportunity: the most-demanded attraction is still the one most venues don't offer.

articles.title: Competitive Socializing's Repeatability Problem: Can the Format Sustain Long-Term Growth?
articles.summary: Competitive socialization venues are growing at 84% annually in the US — nearly eight times the rate of traditional FECs — but industry observers are questioning whether the format can drive repeat visitation over time. Despite strong signals including Level99's $100M growth round, the core challenge is converting first-time novelty seekers into loyal, returning guests. FEC operators considering adding competitive socializing concepts should weigh this repeatability risk carefully before committing capital.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Accelerates $13.3 Billion Indoor Entertainment Center Buildout
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is intensifying a massive $13.3 billion investment in indoor entertainment centers as part of its Vision 2030 diversification strategy. The scale of this buildout represents one of the largest government-backed FEC expansions in history and is reshaping the global supply chain for amusement equipment and attractions. International suppliers and operators should take note of the procurement opportunities and competitive dynamics this creates.

articles.title: SEVEN Tabuk Opens With Cyber Bowling, Indoor Golf, and More as Saudi FEC Rollout Accelerates
articles.summary: SEVEN Tabuk has opened just days after SEVEN Abha, continuing Saudi Arabia's rapid deployment of large-scale indoor entertainment destinations featuring cyber bowling, indoor golf, and diverse attractions. The SEVEN brand is quickly becoming one of the most aggressive FEC rollout stories globally. This pace of new openings underscores the enormous investment pipeline reshaping the Middle East entertainment market.

articles.title: Minnesota Bowling Centers Reinvent Themselves to Stay Competitive
articles.summary: Bowling businesses across Minnesota are evolving beyond traditional lanes, adding food and beverage upgrades, arcade games, and social entertainment elements to attract new demographics. The trend mirrors a national pattern of bowling centers transitioning into full-service FECs to grow per-cap spending and drive repeat visits. Operators in the bowling segment will find this a useful case study in diversification strategies.

articles.title: Semnox and Uplay Complete Six Venue Management Projects Across Benelux Region
articles.summary: Semnox and its partner Uplay have successfully delivered six venue management system implementations across the Benelux region over the past year, covering cashless payments, access control, and game management. The partnership will showcase their combined capabilities at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 in London this September. This is a notable data point for FEC operators evaluating integrated venue management platforms.

articles.title: Six Flags Expands Licensed Haunted Attractions to 29 Venues for 2026 Halloween Season
articles.summary: Six Flags is rolling out an expanded Halloween portfolio featuring 29 new and returning licensed haunted attractions, 196 themed scare zones, and live entertainment across its park network. The scale of IP-licensed seasonal programming signals how large operators are using branded horror content to drive fall attendance. Smaller FEC operators can draw lessons on seasonal theming and IP partnerships to boost Q3-Q4 revenues.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Signs Lease on First Montana Location
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment Centers has signed a lease for its first Montana location, continuing the trampoline park and FEC chain's geographic expansion across the US. Launch has been one of the more active FEC brands in converting vacant big-box retail spaces into entertainment venues. The Montana signing adds to a growing footprint that operators and landlords in secondary markets will want to monitor.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Converts Former Dillard's Department Store Into Denton, TX Fun Zone
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is transforming a shuttered Dillard's department store in Denton, Texas into a large-format FEC, targeting a fall 2026 opening. The project is a strong example of the adaptive reuse trend fueling FEC growth in vacant anchor retail spaces. For FEC developers and landlords, this underscores the ongoing opportunity in second-generation big-box conversions.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Opens in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new FEC billing itself as Texas' largest has opened in Houston, positioning the facility as a major destination in one of the country's most competitive entertainment markets. Large-format FECs continue to raise the bar for guest experience expectations and per-visit spend. Houston operators and regional investors will want to assess how this new entrant reshapes the local competitive landscape.

articles.title: IATP Partners With TheHopeLine to Support Young Employees and Guests at Trampoline Parks
articles.summary: The International Adventure & Trampoline Parks Association has announced a partnership with TheHopeLine, a free 24/7 crisis chat service for students and young adults, making it available to IATP member venues. This is a meaningful step for an industry that employs a large number of young workers and serves youth-heavy guest demographics. FEC and trampoline park operators should review how similar mental health resources can be integrated into their staff and guest support programs.

articles.title: IAAPA Reveals 2026 Hall of Fame Inductees Ahead of Orlando Expo
articles.summary: IAAPA has announced its 2026 Hall of Fame inductees, who will be officially recognized during IAAPA Expo 2026 in Orlando, Florida. The Hall of Fame honors individuals who have made significant and lasting contributions to the global attractions industry. FEC industry professionals attending IAAPA Expo should mark this ceremony as a key networking and recognition moment.

articles.title: Guy Fieri's Downtown Flavortown FEC Opens in Myrtle Beach With Celebrity Ribbon Cutting
articles.summary: FACE Amusement Group and celebrity chef Guy Fieri will officially open Downtown Flavortown at Myrtle Beach Mall on September 10, 2026, combining dining and amusement attractions under a recognizable consumer brand. The opening represents a high-profile example of celebrity IP being leveraged to anchor a family entertainment destination in a tourist market. FEC developers and operators should watch this concept for insights on entertainment-dining hybrid models and celebrity brand licensing.

articles.title: Adventure Landing Closes Raleigh Location After 38 Years in Operation
articles.summary: Adventure Landing, a multi-attraction FEC staple offering go-karts, mini golf, and arcade games, has abruptly shuttered its Raleigh location after 38 years, ending a long run as a local entertainment anchor. The sudden closure highlights the ongoing challenges facing legacy FEC formats that have not fully modernized their offerings. Operators of older multi-attraction venues should view this as a cautionary signal about the need for continuous reinvestment.

articles.title: Bergen County Mega Entertainment Center Goes to Auction — Trampolines, Bowling Lanes, and VR Arena Included
articles.summary: A large multi-attraction entertainment center in Bergen County, NJ is heading to auction, with its inventory including trampolines, bowling lanes, and a virtual reality arena. Auctions of FEC assets offer acquisition opportunities for operators looking to expand or launch venues at reduced capital costs. Equipment buyers and prospective FEC operators in the Northeast should monitor this sale closely.

articles.title: Family Entertainment Group Reaches 100-Location Milestone With Margaritaville at Sea Partnership
articles.summary: Family Entertainment Group LLC is celebrating its 100th location milestone, anchored by a landmark new partnership to bring its entertainment programming aboard Margaritaville at Sea cruise experiences. The milestone reflects strong franchise growth for one of the sector's more active multi-site operators. The cruise partnership also signals an emerging channel for FEC operators to extend their brands beyond fixed real estate.

articles.title: XBOX and BBC Studios to Lead Location-Based Experience Sessions at Brand Licensing Europe 2026
articles.summary: XBOX and BBC Studios will present dedicated sessions on IP licensing for the location-based experiences market at Brand Licensing Europe, taking place October 6-8 in London. The sessions will cover franchise building and practical lessons learned from LBE deployments, offering direct guidance for FEC operators exploring branded IP activations. This is a must-attend event for operators and developers seeking to understand how major entertainment IP holders are approaching the FEC and LBE sector.

articles.title: Fun Spot America Launches Early-Access Season Pass Offer Spanning 16 Months
articles.summary: Fun Spot America is rolling out its first-ever Early Access Season Pass campaign, allowing guests to purchase discounted 2027 season passes now while receiving free access through the remainder of 2026 — delivering up to 16 months of value. The promotion is designed to drive advance revenue commitment and build loyalty ahead of the new year. FEC operators can draw direct inspiration from this approach to early-bird season pass sales as a cash flow and retention tool.

articles.title: Two New Bowling Alleys Set to Open in Western Australia
articles.summary: Two new bowling alley projects are in development in Western Australia, adding to a pipeline of bowling and entertainment venues expanding across the Asia-Pacific region. The openings reflect sustained consumer demand for bowling as an anchor attraction within broader FEC formats. Suppliers and operators eyeing the Australasian market should note the continued growth momentum in this segment.

articles.title: WhiteWater Debuts Helix Twist — World's First Optical Illusion Water Slide
articles.summary: WhiteWater has unveiled the Helix Twist, a water slide using a physically twisting flume profile to alter riders' perception of motion, orientation, and gravity — the first of its kind in the world. The feature debuted at The Land of Legends in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the Dragonfly Jet water slide. While focused on water parks, the innovation points to how sensory-manipulation technology is becoming a differentiator for attraction designers across the broader FEC and entertainment venue space.

articles.title: Former Jersey Shore Drugstore Redeveloped as Family Entertainment Center
articles.summary: A long-vacant drugstore at the Jersey Shore is being converted into a family entertainment center, adding to the trend of retail-to-FEC adaptive reuse projects transforming dead commercial space along tourist corridors. The project reflects broader developer interest in FEC as a productive use for struggling retail real estate. Operators and developers in coastal and tourist markets should note the demand signals this type of conversion represents.

articles.title: Fantasy Island Entertainment Center Construction Begins at Former Ship Bottom CVS Site
articles.summary: Construction has started on a new Fantasy Island-branded entertainment center at a former CVS pharmacy site in Ship Bottom, NJ, continuing the trend of FEC development in repurposed retail locations. The project brings a recognized regional amusement brand to a new format and location type. This is another data point in the accelerating conversion of vacant pharmacy and drugstore real estate into entertainment venues along the East Coast.

articles.title: Calypso's Cove Adds Real JCB Excavator Ride Experience From Diggerland USA
articles.summary: Calypso's Cove in Old Forge, NY has added an Excavator attraction featuring real JCB mini excavators transferred from Diggerland USA, giving guests a hands-on heavy machinery experience. The addition illustrates how smaller regional FECs can differentiate their offering with unique, tactile attractions not found at larger competitors. This type of experiential novelty attraction can be a strong driver of word-of-mouth and social media engagement.

articles.title: Disney Patents Personalized Attraction Recommendation System Based on Guest Preferences and Aversions
articles.summary: Disney has been granted a patent for a system that matches guests to rides based on detailed personal preferences and aversions, going beyond the basic recommendations currently in its park apps. The system uses a processor and user preference database to filter attractions against health conditions, sensory sensitivities, and likes or dislikes. While Disney-scale in ambition, the underlying concept of preference-based guest journey personalization has direct implications for how FEC operators could evolve their digital engagement and app-based wayfinding tools.

articles.title: Mr. Gatti's Pizza Targets Return to Lubbock With New Family Entertainment Center Franchise
articles.summary: Mr. Gatti's Pizza is actively seeking a franchisee to bring its pizza-and-entertainment FEC concept back to Lubbock, Texas, signaling renewed franchise expansion momentum for the brand. The chain combines dining with arcade and entertainment attractions in a format designed to compete in the family dining and entertainment segment. Prospective FEC franchisees and regional operators in Texas should note this as an available franchise opportunity.

articles.title: Hatfield & McCoy Dinner Show Launches New Autumn-Themed Seasonal Production
articles.summary: The Hatfield & McCoy Dinner Feud in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee is introducing a new harvest-themed show running from September 11 through November 5, offering a seasonally differentiated experience for fall visitors to the Smokies. The update illustrates how dinner theater and entertainment attractions can use seasonal programming to maintain relevance and drive repeat visitation throughout the year. FEC operators with show or event components should take note of this seasonal refresh strategy.
